beats.say: The cloud bill doubled after launch.
Cut the cost. But the nightly finance close must never slow down.
beats.label: The catch
beats.head: Cut cost, keep the finance close fast

beats.say: Three ideas: how BigQuery charges, paying only for work, and guaranteed capacity.
beats.label: Station 5.1 · Optimizing resources
beats.head: Know the price. Pay for work. Reserve.

beats.say: First: BigQuery has two ways to pay.
On-demand is like a taxi. You pay for each trip: every byte your query scans.
beats.label: On-demand
beats.head: Like a taxi: pay per byte scanned

beats.say: Editions are like renting a car. You pay for slots, which is compute, by the hour.
beats.label: Editions
beats.head: Like a rental: pay for slots

beats.say: Spiky, small use? Take the taxi. Heavy, steady use? Rent the car.
beats.label: Which one
beats.head: Spiky: on-demand. Steady: Editions.

check.prompt: What does a budget alert do when the spend reaches the limit?
check.why: A budget alerts. A custom quota or maximum bytes billed is what stops the spend.

beats.say: Now, three guardrails that stop a runaway bill.
A custom quota caps bytes per day. Maximum bytes billed stops one big query. And a partition filter can be required.
beats.label: Guardrails

beats.say: The trap: a budget alert does not stop spending. It only sends an email.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: A budget alert does not cap spending.

beats.say: Second: pay for compute only while it works.
A Dataproc cluster that runs all day, for one nightly job, wastes money for 23 hours.
beats.label: The waste
beats.head: Always on, for one nightly job

beats.say: So use a cluster per job. Add Spot workers. Or go serverless.
beats.label: Dataproc

beats.say: For Dataflow batch jobs that can wait, FlexRS is cheaper.
beats.label: Dataflow
beats.head: FlexRS for batch that can wait

check.prompt: The finance close must always have slots. What do you set?
check.why: A baseline is the guaranteed part of a reservation.

beats.say: Third: protect the finance close.
A reservation is a fence around some slots. Production gets its own fence.
beats.label: Reservation
beats.head: A fence around slots

beats.say: A baseline is the part that is always there, guaranteed.
beats.label: Baseline
beats.head: Baseline = guaranteed slots

beats.say: And an assignment says which project uses which fence.
beats.label: Assignment
beats.head: Assignment: project → reservation

beats.say: Idle slots are shared with others. So nothing is wasted.
beats.label: Bonus
beats.head: Idle slots are shared

beats.say: Recap.
Taxi or rental: know how you pay. Set guardrails. A budget only alerts.
beats.label: Station 5.1 · 1 of 2

beats.say: Pay only while compute works. And reserve slots for critical jobs.
beats.label: Station 5.1 · 2 of 2
